profile.campus: Google Central Ohio (New Albany / Columbus-Lockbourne / Lancaster), OH
profile.address: South High Street, Columbus, Franklin County, OH 43137
profile.reading:
This building is part of Google's central Ohio data center footprint, mapped on South High Street in the Lockbourne area of Columbus, Franklin County. Google's own Ohio locations page, fetched this session, does not name individual buildings or addresses within this footprint, so this specific structure is not independently identified beyond its OSM-derived street location.

Google's cloud infrastructure operates as a business of Alphabet Inc. (NASDAQ: GOOGL/GOOG, SEC CIK 0001652044), headquartered at 1600 Amphitheatre Parkway, Mountain View, California. Google's own Ohio data center location page, fetched fresh this session, states the company broke ground in New Albany in 2019 and has since invested more than $20 billion in the state across New Albany, Lancaster, and Columbus, generating $21.7 billion in Ohio economic activity in 2025 and contributing over $16 million in philanthropic giving since 2006.

Ohio's central corridor data center cluster, of which this Columbus-area building is part, has grown rapidly since 2019 alongside major campuses for Microsoft, Meta, and Amazon Web Services, all separately tracked in this registry, though Google's own public materials describe its Ohio footprint in aggregate rather than naming individual buildings, addresses, or per-building capacity figures.

American Electric Power (AEP Ohio) is the principal electric utility serving most of the New Albany and Columbus-area data center market, and has filed with Ohio regulators for new large-load electric tariff structures in response to rapidly growing data center demand in the corridor. New Albany's community authority has used tax-increment financing agreements, and Ohio's state-level data center sales and use tax abatement program, to help anchor the cluster's continued growth alongside Microsoft, Meta, and Amazon Web Services campuses tracked elsewhere in this registry.

reading.body:
Google does not publish the megawatt capacity or square footage of this Lockbourne facility. The site is part of a multi-county Columbus-area campus spanning Franklin, Licking, and Fairfield counties where Google has announced $1.7 billion in combined investment alongside major hyperscale buildout by AWS and Meta in the same corridor. Without a facility-level power figure, its contribution to Ohio's published data center capacity cannot be determined.

Ohio has 76 mapped data center facilities, but only 8 publish power capacity figures totaling 60.4 MW. This campus ranks 9th in the state by published MW, which means it either publishes no figure (placing it outside the top 8) or the ranking reflects regional estimates not confirmed by Google's own disclosures. Google's policy is to report investment and capacity only at the state level, not at individual building addresses or sites.

The Lockbourne facility's relevance to AI scaling depends on unpublished facts: the actual megawatt allocation to this site, the power density it serves, and its share of the broader Ohio investment. For readers assessing whether this campus matters to near-term AI infrastructure, the absence of published specifications makes a direct comparison to disclosed facilities impossible.
